findings.title: The MEGA BEAR strobes between its full art and a solid white silhouette 10 to 14 times a second under rapid fire
findings.evidence: Frames S/strobe/hmg-00400.png to hmg-00407.png (native 480x270, crop 230,60,250,190; S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macbookair-game/f3aa9207-fb8c-45b4-914e-f54b88055d86/scratchpad/harness/shots/review-art), opened as S/sheets/strobe-hmg.png and on S/sheet-findings.png: the sequence is normal, white, white, normal, normal, normal, normal, white. The fixture W/fx/flashcount.js counts frames where e.hitT > 2 (the exact condition at level2_boss.js:737) from frame 300 to 900 (W=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macbookair-game/f3aa9207-fb8c-45b4-914e-f54b88055d86/scratchpad/harness/work/review-art). Results: H.M.G. 14.4 flashes/s, white on 49% of frames. Tractor machine gun 11.7/s (39%). Flame 9.7/s (32%). Pistol 4.4/s (14%). Rockets 2.0/s. Shotgun 0.8/s. The boss covers 14.6k to 17.5k pixels, 11 to 13.5% of the screen (W/out/mask/all.json, m2-5720), and jumps from mean luminance 0.17 to white. findings.repro: node H/harness.mjs render --level 2 --x 5921.6 --frames 905 --god --extra H/work/integrate/fx/fire-hmg.js --extra H/work/integrate/scn.js --extra W/fx/flashcount.js --out /tmp/x.png, then read the FLASH line on stderr. findings.impact: This is the harshest thing on screen, right at the mission's climax. It breaks the three-flashes-per-second limit (WCAG 2.3.1) over a large area: at 3x full screen the boss is about 530x430 px, above the 341x256 small-area allowance. findings.suggestion: In drawBear (level2_boss.js:737) replace `FLASH = e.hitT > 2;` with a rate-limited flash: `if (e.hitT >= 3 && G.t - (e.flashAt == null ? -99 : e.flashAt) >= 20) e.flashAt = G.t; FLASH = G.t - (e.flashAt == null ? -99 : e.flashAt) < 2;`. I checked this in a patched copy (W/flashfix.html, built with mkvariant.mjs and W/edits-flash.json). H.M.G. drops from 14.4 to 3.0 flashes/s and white frames from 49% to 10%. The tractor drops from 11.7 to 3.0/s and the pistol from 4.4 to 1.6/s. Boss hp at frame 900 is identical (323), so the change only affects drawing. review.strengths:
Mission 2 is clearly better than Mission 1 in almost everything an 8-10 year old sees. At every one of the 40 Mission 2 camera positions the frame is richer than the matching Mission 1 frame. Fixes must not break the following.

1. Mission 1 is untouched. Frames at x 400, 1950, 3350 and 4821.6 are pixel-identical to backup/index-before-level2.html, and the built index.html matches src for both missions (0 px difference).
2. Scenery:
   - Granite house with red tiles, a cat on the bench, an opening door, the hórreo, and a fountain with a scallop shell.
   - The Ría with the Cíes Islands, Vigo, boats, seagulls and the Rande bridge.
   - Woods with light shafts, squirrels, a waterfall and wading water.
   - Farm with farmhouse, windmills, corn, vines, a scarecrow, Galician flags and puddles in the rain.
   - Orchard with rainbow, petals, bees and hives.
   - Galician signs (SOUTO, GRANXA, CEREIXAS).
   - Every area has something moving.
3. Culling is nearly perfect: across 2861 camera positions there is one visible pop (art-6).
4. Readability holds up:
   - Hero edge contrast is 2.3-7.1 in Mission 2 against 1.4-4.7 in Mission 1, for both Ines and Mathias.
   - Outlines are consistent.
   - The HUD reads cleanly for SHOTGUN, ROCKETS, FLAME, H.M.G. and the TRACTOR armour and shells, with no overlaps and 3-digit ammo fitting.
   - Item boxes S, R and F are clear.
5. Pixel discipline:
   - Sprites are built from makeSprite, blob and paint with 1 px outlines.
   - Rockets use 32 pre-rotated sprites.
   - Logs and boulders use pre-drawn frames.
   - Every weapon is drawn for level, up, crouch and jump-down aims.
6. The intro is polished: letterbox, VIGO, GALICIA caption with flag, door opening and closing, WHAT A VIEW!, birds and eagles, then a clean hand-over to the HUD.
7. Moments that feel good:
   - Cage bursts: bars fly and the animal hops with hearts.

   - Splashes when wading.
8. Weapons:

   - Rockets: smoke trail.

9. The tractor art is charming: boarding hop, GET IN!, BATTLE TRACTOR!, armour plates flying off, the wreck.

review.strengths:
On-screen tells: all 4,003 attack tells logged in 60 bot runs had the attacker on screen, and none of the 772 hits came from an attacker that was off screen when its tell started. Wind-ups are generous for kids: wolf pounce 26 frames, eagle dive 38 (aim line and reticle), egg 40 plus its fall, bear and robobear rear 39, paw/charge 44, throw 38 plus ~60 frames of flight, MEGA BEAR swipe 35, toss 41 (landing markers ~75 frames before impact), pound 54, lasers 54.

Reacting pays off: the never-dodging harness bot averaged 20.2 hits (median 15.5) with 30% of runs needing continues and 3.3 deaths. The reacting child with 0.25 s reactions averaged 10.9 hits with hops and 7.4 hits walking, 0/20 continues and 0.05 deaths. Only ~2 of the walker's 7.4 hits cost hearts; the rest are tractor armour at the boss.

On foot the MEGA BEAR is fair and readable as long as the child doesn't hug it. The walker took 0.1 on-foot hits per fight over 20 fights: lasers 0/30 (the DUCK!/JUMP! hints work, lab E4), rocks 0/28 (stepping 14 px off a marker is always safe, E3), waves 2/44. Fights last 49-64 s, inside the spec's 45-75 s.

Eagle dives, eggs, bear rears and boulders/logs are all avoidable by stepping away 0.25 s after the tell (labs E7, E8, E1b, E1c).

Cues kids can learn from: 'GET IN!' (tractor boarded in 60/60 runs), 'HELP!' cages (7/7 animals freed in every run), 'GO >' after each lock, pickup texts with voice lines, WARNING and the boss bar.

Mission 2 is not harder than Mission 1 for the same bot (Mission 1: 12/12 runs need continues, 9.4 hits/min in its hardest area). Its toughest stretches are the ROBO BEAR lock (5.9 hits/min never-dodging, 2.2 reacting) and the boss.

All 84 sims (src, identical to index.html) ended with errors [].

These must not break: the tell lengths, the DUCK!/JUMP! hints, the rock markers, and the boss's rests between attacks.
review.coverage:
Covered:
- 84 headless sims (all errors []), in work/review-kids/out-a:
  - Mission 2, seeds 1-20, three bots, with the observer kobs.js (logs attack tells, hit causes, items, idle stretches, weapon use): the never-dodging harness bot, the reacting child kreact.js with the harness hops, and the reacting child walking without hops (KIDS_HOP=false).
  - Mission 1, seeds 1-12, the same observer, never-dodging bot.
  - 3+3 continue-cost runs from x 4460.
  - 6 runs of kreact2.js (better rock-dodge direction).
- Controlled labs on the real code (lab-mb.js, lab-en.js, lab-wp.js, lab-fix.js, lab-e1.js): every MEGA BEAR attack on foot and in the tractor, wolf, eagle, egg, bear and robobear attacks with reaction times, and a weapon time-to-kill/dps table.
- Before/after tests on patched copies built with mkvariant (variant-fix.html: REACH 120 + swipe damage frames 42-49 + wolf skid not hurting; variant-fix2.html: lower charge box + pellet life 24).
- 6 renders in shots/review-kids, opened and cropped: DUCK! over the tractor, the beam through the tractor, the H left behind.
- Checked: index.html contains all 15 src files verbatim, so the src sims represent the built file.

Not covered:
- Audio by ear (K7).
- Real keyboard play in a browser: the Browser pane is reserved for the flow reviewer.
- Hero 1 runs: heroes are cosmetic in the code.
- A reacting bot for Mission 1: the rules are Mission 2 specific, so Mission 1 has only the never-dodging comparison.
- Whether children notice or collect cherries and chestnuts: not measured.
- A tractor rock-dodge lab: only the batch rate, 20/40 hits.
- 'Too scary': judged only from code and renders (tremors, WARNING, a roar and up to 14 px screen shake, comparable to Mission 1's crab; no finding).

Caveats:
- The bots' reactions are idealised (exact 15-frame delay, perfect execution). Real 8-10-year-olds will take more hits, so treat the reacting numbers as a lower bound.
- The harness bot's constant hopping (airborne ~90% of the time) distorts item pickups and some hits.
review.sheet: Telegraph table (60 runs, all tells on screen; window = frames from tell to first hurt frame): wolf pounce 26 (reflex-jump safe window starts at frame 19; walking away always works) | wolf run contact 0 (hit rate 0-3%) | eagle dive 38 (step away: ok; jump/crouch: hit) | egg 40 + fall (step away: ok) | bear/robobear swipe 39 (back off: ok) | charge 44 (walk away: ok; jump-in-place window bear 6-11 / robobear 3-7 frames) | throw 38 + ~60 flight (step out: ok) | MB swipe 35 (from the wall: unavoidable with a reaction of 10+ frames; tractor 207/207 hit) | MB toss 41 (markers 75 frames before landing; stepping 14 px off is safe; tractor 50% hit) | MB pound 54 (jump window 32 frames on foot, 2-6 frames in the tractor) | MB lasers 54 (on foot crouch/jump ok; HIGH unavoidable in the tractor). Hits by bot over 20 seeds: never-dodging 20.2 (30% continue), reacting + hops 10.9 (0%), reacting walker 7.4 (0%). Area hits per minute on foot, never-dodging → walker: home 2.05 → 0.28, woods 5.93 → 2.24, farm (in the tractor, all hits per minute) 2.04 → 0.99, orchard + boss 6.79 → 0.18 (plus 5.4 tractor hits). review.strengths:
- **Mission 1 sound is untouched.** With the logger attached, seed-1 Mission 1 runs on the pre-Mission-2 build and on the current build produce identical sound streams: 3770 tone, noise, music and speech events, 0 differences, including 8 s of the win screen.
- **The built file matches the sources.** index.html gives the same Mission 2 sound stream as src/ (7946 events, 0 differences), so this review applies to what the kids double-click.
- **No clipping anywhere.** In the full renders:
  - Mission 2 seed 1 peaks at -5.4 dBFS (Mission 1: -7.4); the loudest sandbox (shotgun vs MEGA BEAR) at -3.4.
  - At most 14 sounds play at once (Mission 1: 11).
  - All 86,408 logged sound calls have valid values (no NaN, zero or negative).
- **The overall balance matches Mission 1.**

  | | Mission 2 | Mission 1 |
  |---|---|---|
  | whole mix | -32.2 LUFS | -32.6 |
  | music | -37.9 | -38.5 |
  | sound effects | -33.2 | -33.4 |
  | level part, effects vs music (median) | -35.5 vs -36.0 | -37.8 vs -37.3 |

  In the boss fight the effects sit 3-6 dB over the music in both missions.
- **No repeated-sound spam.** No sound restarts on 2 frames or less more than 3 times in a row in any Mission 2 run or sandbox. Effective rate limits:
  - footsteps share one 5-frame slot; wing flaps 8 frames
  - wolf howl 220-frame cooldown; eagle screech 90
  - flame whoosh and hiss timers
- **Nothing plays where it shouldn't.** No game sound on the game-over or win screens except the usual jingle, ticks and fireworks, same as Mission 1. No endless loops or droning sounds.
- **Music hand-overs are correct.** Checked with a forced game over at the boss and with the flow self-test (18/18 ok):
  - boss lock -> bearboss
  - game over -> music stop + 'Game over'
  - continue -> vigo from 4400 + 'Mission start!'
  - second boss lock -> bearboss
  - win -> stop
  - Mission 1 win -> vigo
  - all clear -> 'All missions complete!'
- **The music is well made.** Vigo is a real muineira: 6/8, 16 bars, D mixolydian with no wrong notes, jig rhythms, kick on 1 and 4, hats on 3 and 6, a pickup into the top. Bearboss is 16 bars of D minor, with 51 of 56 strong-beat notes on the chord. Both loop seamlessly and are longer than Mission 1's (16 s and 21.8 s vs 12.8 s and 5.6 s).
- **The voice lines work.** All 7 new lines fire once at the right moment and never cut each other off (no two within 2 s in 5 runs; Mission 1 itself has 'Mission start!' then 'Thank you!' 0.02 s apart).
- **No new sound is both loud and harsh.** The brightest ones (eagle screech 74% above 2 kHz, MB glint, chirps, bear swipe, MB crack) sit at -36 to -51 LUFS-M.
- **Clear signals that work:** the freed jingle (+6.4 dB over the mix, 91%), pickups, egg-bomb beeps (+7.1 dB), the laser charge, the boss roar with 'Mega Bear!' and the death sequence (-20 LUFS-M, like Mission 1's).
review.coverage:
**What I built and ran.** An offline renderer (H/work/review-audio/audiolib.mjs on node-web-audio-api 2.2.0) that copies src/audio.js exactly: the same oscillator, noise and filter setup and the same bus volumes (master 0.6, effects 0.8, music 0.3). With it:

- **Music:** the game's own scheduler (audio.js in a vm, clock advanced 1/60 s per update, tracks read from level2.js) rendered vigo, bearboss, main and boss for two loops each, plus each layer (lead, bass, drums) on its own; the loop seams and the boss hand-over are in the renders. A theory script checked key, rhythm and harmony.
- **Logging:** an --extra logger (sndlog.js) recorded every sound call (time, game file:line, bus), every music note, Music.play/stop and say() during:
  - 5 seeded Mission 2 runs, both heroes
  - 2 Mission 1 runs, and Mission 1 on the legacy build (parity)
  - the built index.html
  - 12 weapon sandboxes: shotgun, rockets, flame, H gun, pistol against wolves, eagles, bear, robobear, MEGA BEAR, and the Mission 1 boss
  - unkillable eagles, to get egg bombs
  - a forced game over at the boss, and the flow self-test
- **Measurements:**
  - peak, clipping, LUFS-style loudness and treble share for whole runs, 1-second steps and every sound on its own (WAVs in H/work/review-audio/wav, 283 files)
  - pile-ups and repeated-sound bursts, overlapping speech
  - whether each warning or reward sound can be heard over the rest of the mix at its real moments (a 1/3-octave band comparison)
  - a laptop-speaker model
  - every proposed fix re-measured on the same events
- **Pictures:** spectrograms and a 94-tile contact sheet in H/shots/review-audio (opened and checked: music vigo and bearboss, handover, intro, full run, sheep rescue, crops).

**Not covered or approximate:**
- Nothing was heard by ear or played in a real browser. Chrome's oscillators are smoother than node-web-audio-api's, so the treble figures are approximate; the levels follow the Web Audio spec.
- The laptop numbers come from a 4th-order 180 Hz high-pass model, not a measured MacBook Air speaker.
- The browser speech voice was not rendered: only timing, overlaps and texts were checked, not its loudness against the mix.
- The audibility test is a simple band-energy comparison, not a hearing model. Its absolute dB figures are indicative; the before/after differences are the solid part.
- Sounds continuing into pause were checked by reading the code only (overlaps the known K13); the bot never pauses.
- The bot never picks up the S in real runs (K1), so the shotgun was measured only in sandboxes.
- The MB ding happened once in 5 runs.
- Audio glitches from frame stalls longer than the music's 120 ms look-ahead cannot be measured headless.
- I did not hand-check every animal call's realism, the title or mission-select sounds (unchanged), or Mission 1 music beyond the parity diff.
